analysis.investment_thesis: Exato is a freshly-listed micro-cap IT services firm priced at 35x earnings on just INR 10 Cr of profit — a valuation that embeds heroic growth assumptions during peak small-cap euphoria. With rising borrowings (6→28 Cr in 2 years), near-zero FCF, and no operating history through a downturn, the risk/reward is deeply asymmetric to the downside.
key_strengths: Strong headline ROE (28.2%) and ROCE (26.5%) on small capital base
Revenue grew 70% over 2 years (73→124 Cr) with margin expansion in FY25
Promoter holding at 54.73% provides reasonable skin-in-the-game
key_risks: P/E of 35x on 10 Cr PAT leaves zero margin of safety if growth disappoints
Borrowings quadrupled (6→28 Cr) while FCF collapsed (10→-20→0); growth is debt-funded
Micro-cap IT-ES is fragmented, low-moat, and vulnerable to client concentration shocks
red_flags: FCF negative/zero for two consecutive years despite reported PAT growth — earnings quality suspect
Recent listing (2025) coinciding with peak small-cap euphoria in India
Financing CF of +19 Cr in FY25 funding the business rather than operations
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Second-level thinking here is straightforward: the market is pricing Exato as a high-quality compounder (35x P/E) while the cash flow statement tells a very different story. FY24 FCF was -20 Cr, FY25 FCF was essentially zero, and the company has been funding working capital and capex via a ballooning debt pile (6→17→28 Cr) and fresh equity (financing CF of +19 Cr in FY25). Reported ROE of 28% looks impressive, but on a 50 Cr equity base with 28 Cr debt, returns are being amplified by leverage on a business that hasn't yet demonstrated self-funding growth. This is the archetypal late-cycle Indian small-cap IPO — strong topline narrative, thin profits, priced to perfection.

Where are we in the cycle? Indian small/micro-caps in 2025-26 have seen the greed pendulum swing to an extreme. A client loss, wage-cost spike, or broader small-cap derating could easily compress this multiple to 12-15x on flat earnings, implying 50-65% downside to roughly INR 150-200. The upside case requires sustained 30%+ growth with margin expansion AND multiple maintenance — three things going right simultaneously. That is not asymmetric risk/reward; it is the opposite. Pass.
